t: Sundiata Keita defeated King Soumaoro Kanté of Sosso at the Battle of Kirina, c. 1235, and became the first Mansa of the Mali Empire.
Most of what is told of his life comes from the Epic of Sundiata, an oral tradition of the Maninka griots, while Ibn Battuta and Ibn Khaldun, writing a century later, confirm that he existed.
The social and political norms of Mali, the Gbara and the Kouroukan Fouga, were first being codified in his reign, and the Manden Charter is listed by UNESCO as intangible cultural heritage.
dyk: The name Sundiata praises him through his mother: it means "the lion of Sogolon", from Sogolon and Jata, lion.
ev: Sundiata is born, son of Naré Maghann Konaté and Sogolon Condé
Sundiata and his allies defeat King Soumaoro Kanté of Sosso at the Battle of Kirina
He becomes the first Mansa of the Mali Empire and sets his capital at Niani
His general Tiramakhan Traore defeats the king of Jolof and conquers the Senegambia and Kaabu
Sundiata dies, by the generally accepted account drowned in the Sankarani River

f.born: c. 1217; son of Naré Maghann Konaté, king of the Mandinka, and Sogolon Condé, according to the oral tradition
f.died: c. 1255; the generally accepted account is that he drowned in the Sankarani River near Niani, though other versions exist
f.role: Prince of the Mandinka; first Mansa (emperor) of the Mali Empire from his victory at Kirina, c. 1235
f.known: Founding the Mali Empire; victory over Soumaoro Kanté at the Battle of Kirina; the Epic of Sundiata; the Kouroukan Fouga or Manden Charter; first ruler to take the title Mansa; capital at Niani
